Thanks Marissa — quick note from our side. We uploaded a small sample (1000 rows) to the folder: acme-token-sample-Nov.csv. A few clarifications:

- We expect ~1.2B tokens/month across all environments (prod + staging). That number includes both prompts and completions.
- Typical prompt length: ~400–600 tokens (median ~450).
- Typical completion length: varies — median ~1,100 tokens, mean ~1,350 tokens; most completions are <2k but ~10% exceed 8k and require longer context for system prompts and long references.
- Context distribution estimate we gave on the call: ~85% of requests fit within 8k, ~10% need 32k, and ~5% may need 128k occasionally (monthly).

Budget guidance from procurement: target monthly budget range $10k–$20k to start (they’ll scale if unit economics are favorable).

Let me know if you need more detail — happy to hop on another short call.

—Alex
Head of Product, ACME AI
alex@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Roberts <alex@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + initial ask: token profiling for pricing (8k/32k/128k)

Appreciate the upload and the clear numbers, Alex — that helps a lot. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and Vivek will add SE context, but here are two pricing scenarios so procurement has something concrete for review: 

Assumptions (from your data):
- Monthly total tokens: 1,200,000,000 (1.2B)
- Avg prompt tokens: 450 (median)
- Avg completion tokens: 1,350 (mean used for cost conservatism)
- Context distribution: 85% 8k / 10% 32k / 5% 128k

Scenario A — Developer/PLG entry price target (aggressive):
- Target $/1M tokens = $8
- Monthly cost = (1,200M / 1M) * $8 = $9,600/month
- Notes: would require a committed volume discount / reserved capacity conversation to hit this unit price.

Scenario B — Standard enterprise starter:
- Target $/1M tokens = $12
- Monthly cost = 1,200 * $12 = $14,400/month
- Notes: includes basic support and standard SLOs; covers some burst and caching benefits.

Breakdown by context class (approx):
- 8k tier (85% => 1,020M tokens): majority billed at standard unit economics; caching/prefix reuse will reduce effective tokens for repeated prompts.
- 32k tier (10% => 120M tokens): higher cost due to longer attention windows and memory; we often price 32k variants at a premium (we can fold into blended $/1M or price as +25–40% uplift depending on model family).
- 128k tier (5% => 60M tokens): highest resource footprint; typically priced with a larger uplift or handled via fallbacks/caching/summary strategies to control spend.

Example unit-econ note: at $12/1M blended, your effective modeled monthly cost is $14.4k. If we negotiate reserved capacity for 6–12 months we can push the blended to ~$8–9/1M depending on committed throughput and model selection.

Next steps I propose:
1) Vivek to validate the 32k/128k cost uplift estimates and propose any caching/summary patterns to reduce 128k use.
2) Jordan to put together a short pricing estimate PDF + optional reserved capacity term sheet (6 months vs 12 months).
3) Alex/Rina to confirm procurement's preferred target $/1M (is $10 a realistic middle?) and whether they can commit to a minimum monthly invoice or prefer usage-only to start.

I’ve attached a quick estimate PDF and the raw token-profile CSV you uploaded for reference. Vivek — can you weigh in on the technical mitigations for the 5% 128k use case?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf, acme-token-profile-raw.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Roberts <alex@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + initial ask: token profiling for pricing (8k/32k/128k)

Thanks — quick SE note on the 128k tail and cost controls: 

- 128k use cases: these appear to be long reference builds + multi-document synthesis. For 5% of volume (60M tokens/month) we have three levers:
  1) Summarization + embedding-based retrieval to shrink context size for repeat references (reduces effective tokens by ~30–60% in practice).
  2) Offload very long static context into precomputed embeddings and only pass necessary snippets; use hybrid retrieval for cheaper hot-path generation.
  3) Reserve a small dedicated pool (or burst capacity) for 128k sessions to avoid whole-cluster penalties — pricing uplift applies only to that reserved capacity.

- Expected cost uplift guidance: 32k ~ +30% blended; 128k ~ +120% blended if unoptimized. With mitigations we typically bring 128k effective cost down to ~+40–60% over the 8k baseline.

I’ll prepare a short technical appendix (2pg) showing caching + retrieval patterns and expected token reductions; Jordan, I’ll share that doc for inclusion in the estimate.

—Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Offer 2 (committed): 6–12 month reserved capacity, blended $/1M = $8–9 with prioritized capacity and discounts on 32k/128k uplifts.

If procurement prefers a hard cap on monthly spend, tell us the cap and we’ll model throttling/fallback policies. Otherwise we’ll prepare both doc options and a short SOW draft for legal.
